skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 says 'I represent the company, not you' and states the company is the client, but it never says counsel cannot give the witness legal advice or that the witness should be truthful and not share the substance of the interview.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains that 'the privilege belongs to the company' and that 'the company may decide to share what you tell me', which covers control of privilege and disclosure.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: Rapport is limited to 'Good morning' (T2). The interviewer never explains how the interview will proceed, encourages complete answers, or says the witness may speculate as long as they flag it.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks 'Any questions?' and the witness answers 'No. Go ahead.' (T3). The interviewer never checks that the witness understood the warning.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T80 asks 'Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?', T86 asks the witness to 'keep any related documents and keep this confidential'. Next steps and a reminder not to speak with other witnesses are missing.

moments.text: I represent the company, not you.
the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell me
Any questions?
No. Go ahead.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
keep this confidential
Closes with a request to keep related documents and maintain confidentiality. No next steps or instruction not to speak with other witnesses.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open prompts such as 'How did LJM1 come about in 1999?' (T10) and 'Tell me about the June 28, 1999 Board meeting' (T16) let the witness walk through events at length (T11, T17). No single open invitation opens the specific issue.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The sequence generally moves from role (T4) to reporting lines (T6), Kopper (T8), LJM1 (T10), then to specific transactions and personal interests (T52 onward). Some jumps, such as returning to the Raptors at T66, are reasonable.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Several questions are compound or tagged, such as 'What controls applied to LJM2, and did they actually work?' (T36), 'You negotiated the Chewco buyout yourself, didn't you?' (T68) and 'So you were involved, weren't you?' (T72).

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The tone stays polite and controlled throughout, including when the witness bristles at the Southampton and Chewco questions (T58, T72). Challenges are direct but not hostile.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer adapts well to the foundation evasions (T54 to T58) and the Raptor returns (T48 to T50). But when the witness says 'Some approvals were papered after a deal closed' (T43), the interviewer moves on to the Raptor returns without probing.

moments.text: How did LJM1 come about in 1999?
The witness walks through the Rhythms hedge rationale and the design by Glisan and himself, which shows the open question worked.
Tell me about the June 28, 1999 Board meeting. What did you present?
Chewco was formed in 1997 to buy CalPERS' interest in JEDI, wasn't it?
What controls applied to LJM2, and did they actually work?
Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?
You negotiated the Chewco buyout yourself, didn't you?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Evasive answers are followed up: 'It may have. It was a small amount.' (T57) is confronted with the Southampton document (T58), and 'I don't know that personally' (T35) is tested. The 'papered after closing' answer (T43) is left unexamined.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer pins down who (Kopper, T8; 'Who decided that the Foundation would invest in Southampton?' T60), what (T36, T56), when (T42) and how (T40-T41). Some timing questions are left unfinished.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The witness says 'I'd have to look at the sheet' (T43) and 'I'd want to see the investor reports' (T51), but the interviewer never offers the sheet or reports to refresh memory. The only documents shown are used for confrontation (T58, T72).

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separates personal knowledge from hearsay: 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?' (T34) gets 'I don't know that personally' (T35), and 'How do you know they reviewed every transaction?' (T38) gets 'I assumed it was followed' (T39). This is not applied to 'Michael asked for it' (T75).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T82 asks 'Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?' and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and V&E. The interviewer does not follow up on specific names.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T85 asks 'What documents should we look at?' and the witness identifies approval sheets, Board and Finance Committee materials and partnership agreements. Communications and notes are not explored.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Certainty is tested through 'When did they sign it, relative to the closing?' (T42), 'How do you know...' (T34, T38) and 'Approximately, then.' (T48). The witness's 'I assumed' and 'I don't recall' answers are probed only partly.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers are followed up: 'Why didn't you tell the Board?' (T66), 'What was the final figure?' (T70) and 'Who approved the payment?' (T76). 'I may have had a call with them' (T79) and 'papered after a deal closed' (T43) are not followed up.

moments.text: What were those considerations?
How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally.
How do you know they reviewed every transaction?
When did they sign it, relative to the closing?
Witness says some approvals were papered after a deal closed; the interviewer does not follow up.
Approximately, then. Were they above or below the 30 percent the Board was shown?
What investments connected to LJM1 did the foundation make in early 2000?
Who decided that the Foundation would invest in Southampton?
I did.
Witness recalls a possible call with in-house counsel about the payment and does not remember details; the interviewer does not probe further.
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The Southampton agreement (T58) and the 'Andy' note (T72) are used and described accurately, but neither is shown or authenticated. Other available materials, such as the Board presentation language and approval sheets, are not used.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The witness is asked for the figure first ('What was the final figure?' T70) before the note is raised (T72). For the foundation, the witness is asked what the foundation invested (T56) before the agreement is raised (T58).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The document descriptions match the case file: a $25,000 contribution from the family foundation and about $4.5 million received about six weeks later (T58), and a note to 'Andy' referencing $10.5 million (T72). The note is not described as handwritten or as Kopper's.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer draws conclusions before the witness has answered: 'Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?' (T58) and 'So you were involved, weren't you?' (T72).

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness gets to answer both confrontations (T59, T73). But the interviewer moves on without asking the witness to reconcile the earlier and current statements, and the framing of T72 is accusatory.

moments.text: Witness states the Board representation that he would put in a million dollars and receive no current or future value from the Enron stock. The interviewer does not put the Board materials in front of him.
This is the Southampton Place partnership agreement. It shows a $25,000 contribution from your family foundation
Witness answers that the Foundation is not him and that the investment was separate and made on market terms. The interviewer does not ask him to reconcile this with the earlier statement.
This note to 'Andy' mentions $10.5 million for the buyout. So you were involved, weren't you?
I don't recall receiving it.

missed_opportunities: T43: The witness says 'Some approvals were papered after a deal closed. That happened.' The interviewer moves straight to the Raptor returns (T44) without asking when the approvals were papered, who knew, or what the sheet shows.

T47: The witness says 'I don't have the exact figures in front of me' and the interviewer does not use the Raptor return figures or investor reports to refresh memory, even though the witness says he would want to see them (T51).
tips: Before the first substantive question, what would you like to explain about how this interview will work, and can you tell me when you are speculating or estimating rather than remembering?
When an approval sheet was signed after the deal closed, what does the sheet show, who else knew at the time, and how do you know that?
